To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

protein kinase C contributes to ANG II desensitization in adult rat cardiac cells by a mechanism that is independent of receptor phosphorylation and is homologous to the desensitization observed for purinergic receptors.
PKC-mediated desenstization of ANGII-induced IP production in rat cardiac fibroblast cultures occurs rapidly, is homologous, and is reversible.
the G protein-linked ANG II receptor in cardiac fibroblastic cells is desensitized by a PKC-dependent mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which ANG II regulates the growth of cardiac fibroblastic cells.
the molecular mechanisms of the ANG II signal.
the role of PKC in the ANG II-induced signaling in cardiac fibroblastic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ANG II-induced PKC-mediated desentization of ANGII signaling in rat CFs is a novel and important mechanism of negative regulation of cardiac fibroblastic responses to ANG II.
PKC is an important mediator of desensitization to the effects of ANG II.
the ANG II signal is terminated rapidly by a negative feedback loop that is mediated by PKC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ANG II activates G(q), which activates phospholipase C, which activates PKC, which inhibits phospholipase activity, and which terminates ANG II responses in rat CFs.
PKC is a negative regulator of ANG II-induced G(q)-phosholipase C- IP(3) activity.
the ANG II-induced PKC-mediated feedback loop is a major determinant of the duration and magnitude of the IP-C(2+) response of CFs to ANGs II and may play a role in the regulation of fibrosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PKC plays a major role in regulating the ANG II signal in rat cardiac fibroblast.
ANG II signaling is rapidly desensitized in rat CFs by PKC-mediated mechanisms.
the ANG II-induced G(q) response in CFs is short-lived because of a PKC-mediated negative feedback loop that is activated within 30 s of ANG II addition and that is resensitized within minutes.
